purpose: Resume Hyksos/Second Intermediate Period Moses research without promoting hypotheses to facts.

secure: Avaris had a large Levantine-derived population and later a Hyksos ruling dynasty.
Seqenenre Tao died violently in the anti-Hyksos conflict and his mummy preserves lethal weapon trauma.
Kamose fought Apepi and Ahmose I ultimately reconquered Avaris.
1 Chronicles 7:20-23 contains Ephraimite deaths involving men of Gath, Ephraim's mourning, and Beriah's birth.
Exodus 13:17 gives avoidance of the Philistine road because of war.
Ezekiel 37 contains both the dry-bones vision and the Judah/Joseph-Ephraim two-stick sign.
Brooklyn Papyrus 35.1446 documents household dependents including many West Semitic names in the relevant broad pre-New-Kingdom social world.
plausible_background: A Levantine-origin child could plausibly have been raised in an Egyptianized elite Avaris household.
An otherwise unattested Hyksos royal daughter in the required generation is plausible given poor preservation of the royal family.
Egyptian-looking names in the Moses/Levitical tradition can preserve Egyptian cultural memory, but do not by themselves identify an Egyptian office or class.
Avaris's political transition may be relevant background for the Exodus motif of a new regime fearing an internally numerous population.
suggestive: Late Manetho/Josephus Hyksos-expulsion traditions structurally resemble parts of an Exodus constellation and show an ancient Jewish Hyksos-Israel association.
Later Jewish traditions about Ephraimites leaving Egypt prematurely may preserve an independent interpretive memory worth tracing.
Seqenenre's real violent death in the relevant war horizon makes him a testable pursuer candidate, but his weapon injuries require a battle model rather than simple drowning.
Shasu-yhw inscriptions are relevant to a southern Yahweh/Seir-Midian/Kenite inquiry but do not identify the Shasu as Exodus Israelites.
unsupported_or_low: Tati, Tani, Ziwat or Herit was Moses's foster mother.
Ephraimites were the Hyksos chariot corps or military backbone.
Ephraimite troops defected from Avaris during Ahmose's conquest.
Ahmose enslaved Hebrews specifically because of an Ephraimite defection.
The Gath casualties of 1 Chronicles occurred around 1550 BCE or left bones visible on Moses's later route.
Ezekiel's dry bones are literally the Gath Ephraimite dead.
Levites were an Egyptian priestly intelligence service.
Senenmut was Moses in the end-Hyksos chronology.

chronology.moses_birth_working: c. 1660-1630 BCE; near 1635 BCE if confrontation is near Seqenenre's death and Exodus 7:7 age 80 is applied
chronology.note: Acts 7 supplies the 40+40 staging; Exodus itself supplies age 80 at confrontation.
